This Writ Petition is filed seeking to issue a writ of Declaration declaring that the Land Acquisition Proceedings initiated under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, in respect of half undivided share of the lands measuring an extent of 4.50 acres, comprised in Survey No.682 and 0.42 acres in Survey No.683 situate at Chenathur Village, Hosur Taluk, Krishnagiri District, deemed to have lapsed in view of Section 24(2) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Re-settlement Act, 2013.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Re-settlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Mr.S.Ramachandran, learned Standing Counsel for TNHB, appearing for the respondents 2 and 3 submitted that already the land was acquired and award was also passed on 30.07.1994 itself and that the amount of compensation was also deposited before the Treasury.

Further, the possession was taken and for the beneficiaries, it was divided as housing sites and more than 64% of house sites have been granted to the beneficiaries and patta also transferred in their names.

3. Since the possession has already been taken and the same has also been used as stated above, the lapse under Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Re- settlement Act, 2013 would not arise.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Re- settlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, there is no merit in the Writ Petition and the same is liable to be dismissed.
4. Accordingly, the Writ Petition is dismissed.
The petitioners are at liberty to work out their remedy for withdrawing the amount of compensation already deposited.
There shall be no order as to costs.
